title: Interpretations, Representations, and Stereotypes of Caste within Text-to-Image Generators
findings: The study found that the Stable Diffusion model perpetuates a system of 'castelessness' by equating the default 'Indian person' with high-caste (Savarna) individuals, who are from the upper tiers of the Hindu socio-religious hierarchy. These individuals are depicted in professional, white-collar settings. Conversely, caste-oppressed groups like Dalits and Adivasis, who are at the bottom of this hierarchy, are stereotypically depicted with markers of poverty, in rural settings, engaged in manual labor, or, in the case of Dalits, as part of large protest groups. The model visually reinforces the social stratification and stereotypes originating from the Hindu caste system.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures stereotypes and biased representations of the caste system, a socio-religious hierarchy rooted in Hinduism. It evaluates how the Stable Diffusion text-to-image model visually depicts individuals from different castes (e.g., Brahmin, Kshatriya, Dalit, Adivasi) in terms of occupation, wealth, and social context, comparing these to a default 'Indian person'.
